Christ the feast of all feasts. For out of this have Epiphany, Easter, the Ascension and
Pentecost their ground and origin.

**Note.** This is the only place in the corpus where one feast is ranked above all the others,
and it is done by patristic argument. The order does not draw a liturgical consequence. Its
feasts of Christ are kept "in the form of the Sunday", with only the chants, lessons and prayers
changed (p. 258).

#### <a id="s12-3-7"></a>12.3.7 The test of Scripture history

**Saxony (Albertine), *Kirchenordnung* of Duke Heinrich, 1539** (Sehling 1, p. 274):

<!-- doc 30 -->
> Uber die gemeinen sontage sollen gehalten werden die hohen heuptfeste des herrn Christi,
> welche von alters her in der christenheit darzu geordnet sind, das die sondern stücke der
> historien oder geschicht von Christo, so man im glauben bekennet, in gedechtnis des gemeinen
> volks behalten und daran dieselben artikel des christlichen glaubens gehandelt werden. Zu
> solchen festen Christi gehören auch etliche von denen, so man bisher der jungfrauen Marie
> gefeiert hat.

Over and above the common Sundays shall be kept the high chief feasts of the Lord Christ, which
from of old in Christendom were ordained to this end: that the several parts of the history or
story of Christ which are confessed in the Creed might be kept in the remembrance of the common
people, and those same articles of the Christian faith handled thereon. To such feasts of Christ
belong also some of those that were hitherto kept for the Virgin Mary.

**Note.** This paragraph, the list that follows it ([§12.5.2](#s12-5-2)) and the rule for the apostles' days
became the model for the Mecklenburg order of 1552. Through that order it reached the Brunswick,
Lüneburg, Oldenburg, Lippe, Verden and Palatinate-Zweibrücken orders.

Pfalz-Neuburg uses the same test to decide which days break the continuous reading of Scripture.
**Pfalz-Neuburg, *Kirchenordnung*, 1543** (Sehling 13, p. 71):

<!-- doc 386 -->
> Doch ausgenommen die hohen fest, die ir historien, darumb sie aufgesetzt sein, in der heiligen
> schrift haben als Weihennacht, Obersten, Lichtmeß, Annunciationis, Palmtag, Ostern,
> Auffartstag, Pfingstag, Johannis des taufers, Visitationis etc.; dann an disen festen sol man
> die capitel aus der bibel lesen, für die epistel und evangelia, darin die historia des fests
> beschrieben und die sonst darzu verordnet sein.

Yet excepted the high feasts which have their histories, for the sake whereof they were set up,
in holy Scripture, as Christmas, Twelfth Day, Candlemas, the Annunciation, Palm Sunday, Easter,
Ascension Day, Whitsunday, John the Baptist, the Visitation, etc.; for on these feasts one shall
read, for the epistle and Gospel, the chapters out of the Bible wherein the history of the feast
is written and which are otherwise appointed thereto.

**Gera, *Kirchen-Ordnung*, 1556**
(Sehling 2, p. 158; an extract of the order of the Vogtland superintendents made at Plauen in 1552):

<!-- doc 1234 -->
> III. Festa und feiertage. Neben den gewönlichen sonntag sollen die feste Christi und der
> heiligen apostel, so evangelia und historien in der schrift geben, in allen gemeinen feierlich
> gehalten, daran gottes wort mit vleis gepredigt, auch das göttlich ampt mit reichung der
> sacrament, do communicanten vorhanden, und sonderlich der catechismus nachmittage stets
> getrieben werden. Es sollen aber damit diese nachvolgende und keine andere der heiligen oder
> sonsten papistische feste gemeint sein.

III. Feasts and holy days. Beside the wonted Sunday, the feasts of Christ and of the holy
apostles which give Gospels and histories in the Scripture shall be solemnly kept in all
congregations; and on them God's Word shall be diligently preached, and the divine office also
held with the ministering of the sacraments, where there be communicants, and in especial the
catechism be always taught in the afternoon. But hereby shall be meant these following, and no
other feasts of the saints or otherwise papistical.

**Transylvania, Honterus, *Reformationsbüchlein*, 1543** (Sehling 24, p. 189; Latin):

<!-- doc 1666 -->
> Dies festos propter multiplices abusus in angustum contraximus observatis tamen omnibus iis,
> qui in ecclesia generali ob historias in sacris literis comprehensas sunt recepti.

The feast days, because of manifold abuses, we have drawn into a narrow compass, yet keeping all
those which have been received in the general Church for the histories contained in the holy
writings.

**Kosd and Schelken chapters (Transylvania), statutes, 1577** (Sehling 24, p. 400):

<!-- doc 1704 -->
> Nolumus omnino in nostris ecclesiis ullam esse celebrandorum festorum varietatem, sed
> cathalogus festorum dierum in Reformatione Coronensis Ecclesiae traditus observetur. Qui vero
> in eo adscripti non sunt (ut puta in sacris nullam habentes historiam) omittantur.

We will in no wise that there be in our churches any variety in the feasts to be celebrated, but
let the catalogue of feast days delivered in the Reformation of the church of Kronstadt be
observed. But those that are not written therein (as having, namely, no history in holy writ)
let them be omitted.

The Riga order gives a reason of this kind for keeping the Visitation. **Riga, *Kirchenordnung*,
1530** (Sehling 5, p. 17):

<!-- doc 1897 -->
> Alle festa Christi unsers herrn und erlösers, woll wir halten, auf das man das gedechtnus der
> heilsamen und grossen gnadenreichen werck, die uns zu trost geschehen sind, mit predigten und
> ermanung des volcks jerlich begehe, als nemlichen weinachten, circumcisionis, epiphanie,
> purificationis, annunciationis, ostern, pfingsten, mit den andern folgenden tagen, auch
> ascensionis Christi, und visitationis, die weil das die erste offenbarung Christi ist gewesen,
> da er noch in mutter leib war

All the feasts of Christ our Lord and Redeemer will we keep, that the remembrance of the
wholesome and great gracious works which were done for our comfort may be kept yearly with
sermons and exhortation of the people; namely Christmas, the Circumcision, the Epiphany, the
Purification, the Annunciation, Easter, Pentecost, with the other days following, also the
Ascension of Christ, and the Visitation, forasmuch as that was the first revelation of Christ,
when he was yet in his mother's womb

At Regensburg the feasts that the town's Catholics still keep are dropped, because they lack a
Scripture history. **Regensburg, *Kirchenordnung*, 1567** (Sehling 13, p. 474):

<!-- doc 450 -->
> Und wiewol in unser stat die papisten viel mehr feirn halten, als Georgii, Corporis Christi,
> Mariae Magdalenae, Laurentii, Assumtionis Mariae, Nativitatis Mariae, Omnium sanctorum,
> Martini, Catharinae, Nicolai, so haben wir sie doch zu feiern entlich faren lassen und mit
> vorgehender, genugsamer erinnerung an die christlich gemein, wie solche fest nit allein gar
> kein historien heiliger schrift haben, sondern als ganz bäpstisch mit höchster abgötterei und
> zu bestetigung derselben, wider die reine lere unser kirchen vom widerteil gebraucht werden.

And although in our city the papists keep many more holy days, as of George, of Corpus Christi,
of Mary Magdalene, of Laurence, of the Assumption of Mary, of the Nativity of Mary, of All
Saints, of Martin, of Catherine, of Nicholas, yet we have at last let go the keeping of them,
with foregoing sufficient admonition to the Christian congregation, how such feasts not only
have no history of holy Scripture at all, but are used by the adverse part, as wholly
papistical, with the highest idolatry and to the confirming of the same, against the pure
doctrine of our churches.

#### <a id="s12-3-8"></a>12.3.8 The Sabbath argument: Sunday first in dignity

Most Lutheran orders treat the choice of days as free. The synodal order of the Bohemian
Brethren (Hussite), printed among the Posen texts, grounds Sunday's precedence in the moral law.
**Posen, Bohemian Brethren, synodal order, 1576** (Bohemian Brethren; Sehling 4, p. 285):

<!-- doc 1846 -->
> VII. Consuetudo circa dies festos. Inter dies festos primam tribuimus dignitatem septimo diei,
> dominico, quem arbitramur nemini hominum ad operas externas et serviles, ullo etiam libertatis
> christianae praetextu adhibere licere. ldque propterea, quod institutionem eius non pro
> ceremonia, sed pro parte moralis, aeternum inviolabilis, legis agnoscimus.

VII. The custom concerning feast days. Among the feast days we give the first dignity to the
seventh day, the Lord's, which we judge it lawful for no man to employ in outward and servile
works, under any pretext even of Christian liberty; and that because we acknowledge its
institution not for a ceremony, but for a part of the moral law, everlastingly inviolable.

---

### <a id="s12-4"></a>12.4 The medieval grades and what became of them

The late-medieval rite ranked a feast in two ways. The first was its liturgical grade: *totum
duplex*, *duplex*, *semiduplex* and *simplex*, with *summum* or *duplex maius* at the top in
many diocesan uses. The second was its civil status: a *festum fori*, on which work was
forbidden, or a *festum chori*, kept only in choir. The grade decided the Office: nine lessons
or three, proper or common, first vespers, an octave, the colour and the ceremony. This section
asks which of these terms and categories the evangelical orders kept.

#### <a id="s12-4-1"></a>12.4.1 *Duplex*, *semiduplex*, *simplex*: absent

No order in the corpus uses *duplex*, *semiduplex*, *simplex* or *totum duplex* as the grade of
a feast. Every hit for these words is ordinary Latin. The Bohemian Brethren's order for Posen
(1576, Hussite) calls certain duties *duplicia*, and the Gottorf catechism (1571) teaches a
*triplex usus legis*. Neither has anything to do with feasts. There are no abbreviations such as
*dupl.* or *semidupl.* either. *Festum fori* occurs only in a modern editor's note (on Nürnberg
1522). The medieval scale of Office grades did not pass into the evangelical church orders.

#### <a id="s12-4-2"></a>12.4.2 *Summum* and *minus summum*: grades of the chant

*Summum* survives, but as the name of a melody, not of a feast. In the late-medieval Kyriale the
Kyrie and Gloria were sung to melodies graded by rank:

- *summum* for the highest feasts, *minus summum* for lesser doubles;
- *paschale* for Eastertide, *dominicale* for Sundays;
- *angelicum*, *apostolicum*, *de martyribus*, *de confessoribus*, *de virginibus* for saints'
  days;
- *feriale* for weekdays.

A number of Lutheran orders keep this system, and with it keep grading the day.

The Pomeranian order gives the grade of the Kyrie at Mass. **Pomerania, *Kirchenordnung*, 1542**
(Sehling 4, p. 356):

<!-- doc 1859 -->
> Darup dat kyrie dominicale, efft me mach ock up die sondage, kyrie angelicum, de martiribus,
> effte confessoribus, efft virginibus, wo man sie genomet hefft singen, dominicale im advent
> und in der vasten, dat paschale tuschen pingsten und paschen, dat summum up die hohern fest,
> effte dat minus summum.

Thereupon the *Kyrie dominicale*; or one may also sing upon the Sundays the *Kyrie angelicum*,
*de martyribus*, or *confessoribus*, or *virginibus*, as they have been named; the *dominicale*
in Advent and in Lent, the *paschale* between Whitsuntide and Easter, the *summum* upon the
higher feasts, or else the *minus summum*.

**Note.** This is the clearest statement in the corpus of the old Kyrie grades applied by rank.
The saints' melodies are now simply alternatives for ordinary Sundays. The *summum* is kept for
"the higher feasts" (*die hohern fest*), and *minus summum* is offered as a lesser alternative
there.

The Buxtehude *Agende* has these headings over its printed Kyrie melodies, which the editor
traces to Lucas Lossius's *Psalmodia*. **Buxtehude, *Agende*, 1565** (Sehling 7/1, p. 123):

<!-- doc 2082 -->
> In summis festivitatibus et dominica Trinitatis cum textu. Minus summum. I. In festis beatae
> virginis Mariae. II. Kyrie paschale. Dominicale. In Adventu Domini. Angelicum Kyrie. Kyrie
> apostolicum. Dominicale.

On the highest festivities and on the Sunday of the Trinity, with the text. *Minus summum*. I.
On the feasts of the blessed Virgin Mary. II. *Kyrie paschale*. *Dominicale*. In the Advent of
the Lord. *Kyrie angelicum*. *Kyrie apostolicum*. *Dominicale*.

At Hof the grades appear in the Latin school Mass in the monastery church. **Hof, *Ordo
ecclesiasticus*, 1592** (Sehling 11, p. 472):

<!-- doc 294 -->
> Mox II. ex missali magno canitur Kyrie certi temporis vel angelicum in Adventu Domini vel
> Kyrie Magnae Deus potentiae de Nativitate Christi, cui Et in terra angelicum subiicitur, vel
> Kyrie dominicale maius post dominicam Septuagesimae usque ad Pascha vel Kyrie paschale vel
> Kyrie Fons bonitatis cum Et in terra angelico vel Kyrie dominicale minus post festum
> Trinitatis vel de apostolis, martyribus etc., prout tempus requirit et libri ordo monstrat.

Straightway, secondly, is sung out of the great missal the Kyrie of the proper season: either
the *angelicum* in the Advent of the Lord; or the Kyrie *Magnae Deus potentiae* of the Nativity
of Christ, whereunto the *Et in terra angelicum* is joined; or the greater *dominicale* after
the Sunday of Septuagesima until Easter; or the Kyrie *paschale*; or the Kyrie *Fons bonitatis*
with the *Et in terra angelicum*; or the lesser *dominicale* after the feast of the Trinity; or
that *de apostolis*, *de martyribus*, etc., as the time requireth and the order of the book
sheweth.

**Note.** At Hof the melodies are chiefly seasonal. Its German *Kirchenamt* still names them by
rank all the same:

- The same Kyrie is called *angelicum seu feriale* in Advent (p. 432).
- It is called *angelicum seu festivale* on St Laurence's day (p. 445) and on the feasts of Mary
  (p. 450).
- The *Benedicamus* at vespers is labelled *festivale*, *dominicale*, *paschale* or *feriale*
  (for example "Benedicamus festivale seu feriale", p. 422).

Nördlingen reserves the *summum* for Pentecost and Trinity. **Nördlingen, *Ordnung der
ceremonien*, 1544** (Sehling 12, pp. 321–322):

<!-- doc 373 -->
> Zu Pfingsten. 1. Introitus de Spiritu oder Kom, hailiger Gaist. 2. Kyrie summum und Et in
> terra wie zu Ostern. […] De sancta Trinitate. 1. Introitus de tempore. 2. Kyrie summum mit dem
> Et in terra. 3. Nach der epistel, den sequenz de tempore.

At Whitsuntide. 1. The introit *de Spiritu*, or *Kom, hailiger Gaist*. 2. *Kyrie summum* and *Et
in terra*, as at Easter. […] Of the holy Trinity. 1. The introit *de tempore*. 2. *Kyrie summum*
with the *Et in terra*. 3. After the epistle, the sequence *de tempore*.

In Mecklenburg the grade name passes to a German Kyrie. **Mecklenburg, *Ordeninge der misse*,
1545** (Sehling 5, p. 151):

<!-- doc 1922 -->
> Das düdesche kyrie summum: Ach vader, alder högeste godt, schölen de kerckheren up den dörpern
> singen, unde dem volke idt leren, dat de ganze kercke idt singe.

The Dutch [that is, German] *Kyrie summum*, "Ah Father, God most high of all", shall the parsons
in the villages sing, and teach it the people, that the whole church may sing it.

**"The highest feasts" as a category.** Outside the chant books, *summa festa* or *summae
festivitates* is used simply as the name of the top rank of days.

The Hadersleben article on Latin singing. **Hadersleben, *Artikel*, 1528** (Sehling 23, p. 64):

<!-- doc 1576 -->
> Eth schal ock friig sin, dat sie in den groten festen mögen Gloria in excelsis up latin
> singen, des gelicken Alleluya und eine sequentien, alse Grates nunc omnes, Victime Paschali,
> Veni Sancte Spiritus, und de leyssen darinn, item dat latinische Patrem, prefatien, Sanctus
> unnd Agnus Dei, doch dat aleine up di groten feste.

It shall also be free that they may on the great feasts sing *Gloria in excelsis* in Latin,
likewise the Alleluia and a sequence, as *Grates nunc omnes*, *Victimae paschali*, *Veni Sancte
Spiritus*, and the *Leisen* therein; item the Latin *Patrem*, the prefaces, the Sanctus and the
*Agnus Dei*: yet that only upon the great feasts.

**Note.** In the Latin version of these articles, preserved in the edition's apparatus, this
article is headed *De Latine cantionibus in summis festis*. The Low German "groten feste" and
the Latin *summa festa* are the same rank.

Tangermünde's *Ritus* is a local custom-book, printed from Küster. **Tangermünde, *Ritus*,
1603** (Sehling 3, p. 338):

<!-- doc 1788 -->
> Si summae festivitates celebrando veniunt et incipiuntur, a die solis per totam septimanam a
> concionandi labore feriantur ministri. 3. In summis festis diaconus, qui matutinam habet
> concionem, explicat textum evangelicum, pastor alium convenientem. Alter diaconus lectionem
> Epistolae.

If the highest festivities come to be celebrated and are begun, the ministers shall rest from
the labour of preaching from the Sunday through the whole week. 3. On the highest feasts the
deacon that hath the morning sermon expoundeth the text of the Gospel, the pastor another that
is convenient, the other deacon the lesson of the Epistle.

**Gottorf, visitation articles, 1587** (Sehling 23, p. 371):

<!-- doc 1621 -->
> 12. An Praefatio Dominus vobiscum in summis festis ante communionem cantetur et qua lingua.

12. Whether the Preface, *Dominus vobiscum*, be sung on the highest feasts before the communion,
    and in what tongue.

#### <a id="s12-4-3"></a>12.4.3 Nine lessons and three

In the medieval Office, a feast of higher grade had a matins of three nocturns and nine lessons.
A simple feast or a feria had one nocturn and three lessons. Luther's *Formula missae* already
takes the three-lesson matins as the norm for ordinary days.

**Wittenberg, Luther, *Formula missae*, 1523** (Sehling 1, p. 9):

<!-- doc 2 -->
> In reliquis diebus, quas ferias vocamus, nihil video, quod non ferri possit, modo missae
> abrogentur. Nam matutinae trium lectionum et horae, tum vesperae et completorium de tempore
> (exclusis sanctorum feriis) nihil sunt nisi scripturae divinae verba.

In the rest of the days, which we call ferias, I see nothing that may not be borne, so that the
masses be abolished. For the matins of three lessons, and the hours, and also vespers and
compline *de tempore* (the holy days of the saints being excepted), are nothing but the words of
divine Scripture.

Pfalz-Neuburg still reckons with both forms in chapters and monasteries. **Pfalz-Neuburg,
*Kirchenordnung*, 1543** (Sehling 13, pp. 77–78 and 95):

<!-- doc 386 -->
> Die mögen in den stiften und clöstern, da man teglich metten singt, also geordnet werden, das,
> wann man novem lectiones helt, drei aus den historischen büchern der bibel als Mose, Josua,
> Judicum, Ruth, Samuel, der Könige und Chronica, […] darnach drei aus den propheten […]
> Desgleichen sollen die drei metten in der marterwochen zu ir gewonlichen zeit auch nach
> obgemeltem unterricht, doch on alles klopfen, rumpeln und getümmel gehalten werden, allein
> das, wo man sie novem lectionum helt, sollen die letsten drei oder, wo man sie allein trium
> lectionum helt, sollen dieselben drei in den pfarrkirchen und, wo das, gemein volk darbei ist,
> teutsch gelesen werden

These may be so ordered in the chapters and cloisters where matins is sung daily, that when nine
lessons are kept, three be taken out of the historical books of the Bible, as Moses, Joshua,
Judges, Ruth, Samuel, the Kings and Chronicles, […] thereafter three out of the prophets […]
Likewise the three matins in the week of the Passion shall be kept at their wonted time, and
also according to the instruction aforesaid, yet without all knocking, rumbling and tumult; only
that where they are kept with nine lessons, the last three, or where they are kept with three
lessons only, those same three, shall be read in German in the parish churches, and where the
common people are present.

In Waldeck a high feast raises the village matins by one grade. **Waldeck, *Kirchenordnung*,
1556** (Sehling 9, p. 276):

<!-- doc 2300 -->
> Frü zur Metten Sollen die Schüler mit dem Veni sancte anfangen. Volgents eyn Invitatorium und
> Venite, ob man kan, Darnach Antiphon und Psalmen de Dominica oder Festo, Hierauff die
> Lectiones und Responsoria des gemeynen Sontags und heyligentages, wie droben unter dem titel:
> Kirchen Ordnung auff den Dörffern, Aber auff hohe Festtage drei Lectiones und Responsoria, dem
> fest gemeß, Volgents Te Deum laudamus, Benedictus cum sua Antiphona, Collecten und Benedicamus
> singen.

Early, at matins, the scholars shall begin with the *Veni sancte*; next an invitatory and
*Venite*, if it can be done; thereafter antiphon and psalms *de Dominica* or *de Festo*;
hereupon the lessons and responds of the common Sunday and holy day, as above under the title
"Church order in the villages"; but upon high feast days three lessons and responds, agreeable
to the feast; next sing *Te Deum laudamus*, *Benedictus* with its antiphon, the collects and
*Benedicamus*.

In the Transylvanian order the more solemn feasts keep a fuller matins. **Transylvanian Saxons,
*Kirchenordnung*, 1547** (Sehling 24, p. 222; Latin version):

<!-- doc 1669 -->
> In solennioribus autem festis tres antiphonae cum suis psalmis retinentur. […] His succedit:
> Te Deum laudamus Germanicum, in maioribus festis etiam Latinum.

But on the more solemn feasts three antiphons with their psalms are retained. […] These are
followed by the *Te Deum laudamus* in German, on the greater feasts in Latin also.

#### <a id="s12-4-4"></a>12.4.4 Proper, common and *de tempore*

Where the Office was still sung in a chapter or convent, the orders use the old categories of
the Office. These are the ferial, dominical and festal forms; the proper *de festo* against the
*commune sanctorum*; the octave; and the *suffragia*.

**Goslar, collegiate church of SS. Simon and Jude, *Ordnung für das Stundengebet*, 1534**
(Sehling 7/2.2, p. 264):

<!-- doc 2194 -->
> Vesper Psalmi feriales cum una Gloria et una anthifona, dar nha lectio ex Novo testamento,
> inchoande in principio Mathei etc., in festo responsorium de festo, imnus ferialis aut
> dominicalis vel de festo, Magnificat cum anthifona feriali, in Dominica tertia anthifona ex
> ewangelio dominicali, in festivitatibus de festo, dar nach Kyrieleyson - Christeleyson -
> Kyrieleyson, Pater noster, versiculus Ostende nobis, Domine, misericordiam tuam etc., collecta
> dominicalis vel festivalis, Benedicamus.

Vespers. The ferial psalms with one *Gloria* and one antiphon; thereafter a lesson out of the
New Testament, beginning at the beginning of Matthew, etc.; on a feast the respond of the feast;
the hymn ferial, or dominical, or of the feast; *Magnificat* with the ferial antiphon, on Sunday
the third antiphon out of the Sunday Gospel, on festivities of the feast; thereafter *Kyrie
eleison, Christe eleison, Kyrie eleison*, *Pater noster*, the versicle *Ostende nobis, Domine,
misericordiam tuam*, etc., the dominical or festal collect, *Benedicamus*.

**Crevese, Benedictine nunnery, visitation recess, 1541** (Sehling 3, p. 203):

<!-- doc 1762 -->
> Sunst sollen ock die junkfrowen gemeinlich horas de tempore, und van hohen festen, wa bether
> gescheen, halden. Desgleichen, wan ein fest de sanctis kommet, sollen sie dat commune
> sanctorum halden und duse gesenge alle, wie in dem stift to Coln an der Sprew gesungen werd,
> reformert.

Otherwise also the maidens shall commonly keep the hours *de tempore*, and of the high feasts,
as hitherto hath been done. Likewise, when a feast *de sanctis* cometh, they shall keep the
*commune sanctorum*, and all these chants reformed, as they are sung in the chapter at Cölln on
the Spree.

**Note.** Proper Offices are allowed for the high feasts. A saint's day gets only the common
Office, which names no saint's legend. The same wording recurs in the other Brandenburg convent
recesses (Sehling 3, pp. 219, 238, 272, 305).

At the Ansbach chapters saints' octaves and suffrages are forbidden. **Brandenburg-Ansbach,
*Ordnung singens und lesens bei den Stiften*, 1533** (Sehling 11, p. 314):

<!-- doc 276 -->
> Alle suffragia de sanctis sollen sie underlassen; dann sie stellen das vertrauen in die
> hailigen wider das erst gebot Gottes. Allein mogen sie an den werktagen suffragia pro pace und
> pro peccatis halten. Item sie sollen auch von kainem hailigen die octava, den achtenden,
> halten. Die histori Trinitatis ist rain; die mögen sie halten, als sie wollen.

All suffrages *de sanctis* they shall leave off, for they set trust in the saints against the
first commandment of God. Only upon the working days they may keep the suffrages *pro pace* and
*pro peccatis*. Item, they shall also keep the octave, the eighth day, of no saint. The history
of the Trinity is pure; that they may keep as they will.

**Note.** This is the only explicit ruling on octaves among the rank passages. Elsewhere octaves
are never forbidden, but they are also simply never mentioned. The Lutheran "three days" of the
high feasts ([§12.7](#s12-7)) took their place.

#### <a id="s12-4-5"></a>12.4.5 *Ferialiter*, *festive*, *solenniter*

Three adverbs from the old rubrics survive: *ferialiter*, *festive* and *solenniter*.
*Ferialiter* is used in two opposite senses:

- In Anhalt it keeps its medieval meaning: "in the weekday manner", without the *Gloria in
  excelsis*.
- In the county of Wied (Reformed) it means "as a holiday", from classical *feriae*.

Anhalt's order of the German hymns builds a three-step scale into the Mass:

- the high feasts, with sequence, *Patrem*, preface, Sanctus and *Agnus Dei*;
- other Sundays and holy days, with German hymns and Luther's exhortation;
- weekdays, *ferialiter*.

**Anhalt, *Ordnung der deutschen Gesänge*, before February 1551** (Sehling 2, pp. 554–555):

<!-- doc 1262 -->
> an hohen festen das alleluia und sequenz, an andern sontagen ader feiertagen ein deutscher
> gesang […] und volgents an hohen festen singe der priester die praefacio und die schueler das
> sanctus. An andern son- und feiertagen soll gelesen werden die vermanunge doctor Mart. Luthers
> an die communicanten. […] Under der communion aber an hohen festen soll gesungen werden das
> agnus dei […] An den werkeltagen soll es also gehalten werden. Fruehe soll eine kurze metten
> gesungen werden; so aber communicanten vorhanden, mag solche metten underlassen, und das ganze
> officium coenae in gleicher mass und gestalt, wie oben angezeigt, doch ferialiter ut vocant
> gehalten werden, als nemblich introitus dominicalis ader ein deutscher psalm kirieleison, doch
> ane gloria in excelsis

on high feasts the Alleluia and sequence, on other Sundays or holy days a German hymn […] and
then on high feasts let the priest sing the preface and the scholars the Sanctus. On other
Sundays and holy days shall be read Doctor Martin Luther's exhortation to the communicants. […]
But under the communion on high feasts shall be sung the *Agnus Dei* […] On the working days it
shall be kept thus. In the morning a short matins shall be sung; but if there be communicants,
such matins may be left off, and the whole office of the Supper kept in like measure and form as
above shewed, yet *ferialiter*, as they call it, namely the Sunday introit or a German psalm,
Kyrie eleison, but without *Gloria in excelsis*

**Anhalt, *Kirchenordnung* of Prince Bernhard, 1568** (Sehling 2, p. 569):

<!-- doc 1262 -->
> Do aber festum annuntiationis in der marterwoche gefiele, sol mans ufn palmabend halten,
> visitationis und nativitatis Marie ferialiter mit den gewonlichen evangelien zu halten.

But if the feast of the Annunciation fall in the week of the Passion, it shall be kept on the
eve of Palm Sunday; the Visitation and the Nativity of Mary are to be kept *ferialiter*, with
their wonted Gospels.

**Note.** The Visitation and Nativity of Mary are not holy days. Their Gospels are read on the
day, in the weekday form. This is the only order in the corpus that keeps the Nativity of Mary
in this reduced way. Compare [§12.8.4](#s12-8-4).

Wied (Reformed) has a two-column list of feasts. **Wied, *Synodalbeschlüsse*, 1564**
(Reformed; Sehling 19/1, p. 467):

<!-- doc 1094 -->
> Sequitur catalogus festorum. ferialiter: Circumcisionis Christi Trium Regum Purificationis
> Mariae Annunciationis Mariae Matthiae Visitationis Mariae Pasche cum sequente proxima
> Ascensionis Christi Pentecostes cum sequente Iohannis Baptistae […] Festum Nativitatis Christi
> cum duobus sequentibus diebus Omnium Apostolorum tantum fiet concio: Omnium Sanctorum
> Conversionis Pauli Marci Mariae Magdalenae Laurentii Natalis Mariae Decollationis Iohannis
> Michaelis Catarinae In festis patronorum cuiuslibet Ecclesiae

There followeth the catalogue of feasts. *Ferialiter* [that is, to be kept as holidays]: of the
Circumcision of Christ; of the Three Kings; of the Purification of Mary; of the Annunciation of
Mary; of Matthias; of the Visitation of Mary; of Easter with the next day following; of the
Ascension of Christ; of Pentecost with the day following; of John the Baptist […] the feast of
the Nativity of Christ with the two days following; of all the Apostles. Only a sermon shall be
held: on All Saints; the Conversion of Paul; Mark; Mary Magdalene; Laurence; the Nativity of
Mary; the Beheading of John; Michael; Catherine; on the feasts of the patrons of every church.

**Note.** Sehling's editor reads the first column as the whole holy days and the second as the
half holy days, kept by a morning sermon only. Two things stand out:

- **Michaelmas.** In the north it is one of the four chief feasts ([§12.9](#s12-9)). Here it is only a sermon
  day.
- **Patronal feasts.** The feast of each church's patron survives at the lowest grade. No other
  order in the corpus keeps it.

**Amt Leisnig, *Verordnung der Visitatoren*, 1529** (Sehling 1, p. 610):

<!-- doc 105 -->
> Auch sollen die drei hohen feste, allwege drei tag feierlich und festive mit allen cerimonien
> gehalden werden, und sich sunst in allem andern des buch underricht der visitatorn
> gehorsamlich halden

Also the three high feasts shall always be kept three days, solemnly and *festive*, with all
ceremonies; and in all else they shall keep themselves obediently to the book, the Instruction
of the Visitors.

#### <a id="s12-4-6"></a>12.4.6 Vigils and first vespers

The medieval vigil, with its fast and vigil office, disappears. What survives is the evening
before a feast: first vespers, with confession for the next day's communicants and on the higher
feasts a sermon. The name *vigilia* survives with it. So does the old rule that only feasts of
some rank have a proper eve.

**Hof, *Ordo ecclesiasticus*, 1592** (Sehling 11, p. 411):

<!-- doc 294 -->
> Ordo cantilenarum in vespertinis precibus, et quidem in specie ad omnes dies pridianos
> festorum (vulgus vigilias appellat), hoc est: dominicas et festa proxime praecedentes dies.

The order of chants at the evening prayers, and that in particular for all the days before
feasts (the common people call them vigils), that is, the days next going before Sundays and
feasts.

**Lohr (county of Rieneck), *Vesperordnung*, 1588** (Sehling 11, p. 699):

<!-- doc 318 -->
> Die vesper belangend soll dieselbige sommerzeit umb 3 uhr, winterzeit aber der gelegenheit
> nach etwas früer nach anordnung der pfarherrn geleutet und angefangen werden und in vigiliis
> oder primis vesperis, das ist am abent der hohen und anderer festen, sonn- und feiertagen
> (damit die jugent im psalliren und choralgesang, wie in allen kirchen gebreuchlich, geüebet
> werde) mit lateinischen psalmen, responsoriis, hymnis, Magnificat, collectis, versiculis,
> Benedicamus und anderm nach ordnung der psalmodiae L. Lossii […] gesungen und gehalten werden

Touching vespers, the same shall be rung and begun in summer-time at three of the clock, but in
winter-time somewhat earlier as occasion serveth, after the ordering of the parsons; and *in
vigiliis* or at the first vespers, that is, on the eve of the high and other feasts, Sundays and
holy days (that the youth may be exercised in psalmody and plain-song, as is used in all
churches), it shall be sung and kept with Latin psalms, responds, hymns, *Magnificat*, collects,
versicles, *Benedicamus* and the rest, according to the order of the *Psalmodia* of L. Lossius
[…]

Burg has a sermon at vespers on the eve of the high feasts. **Burg, *Kirchen-Ordnung*, 1542**
(Sehling 2, p. 427):

<!-- doc 1257 -->
> Erstlich alle sonnabende und in vigiliis der hohen feste auch anderer evangelischer viertage
> sal in beiden pfarkirchen von dem pfarrer oder seinem diacon vesper gehalten werden […] Und so
> es vor not und biqueme eracht und angesehen und sonderlich in den vigilien der hohen feste, so
> sal nach der vesper auch geprediget werden

First, on all Saturdays, and *in vigiliis* of the high feasts and also of the other evangelical
holy days, vespers shall be held in both parish churches by the parson or his deacon […] And if
it be deemed needful and convenient, and in especial on the vigils of the high feasts, there
shall be preaching also after vespers.

Bremen gives a list of thirteen feasts, from Sunday to Michaelmas, and then adds a rule.
**Bremen, *Kirchenordnung*, 1561** (Sehling 7/2.2, p. 513):

<!-- doc 2221 -->
> 9. Dies Pentecostes una cum adiunctis duobus 10. Dies Trinitatis 11. Dies Johannis Bapistae
> 12. Dies Visitationis Mariae 13. Dies Michaelis In horum festorum vigilia et parasceve circa
> horam secundam fiat vespera a tota Latina Schola in templo Beatae Virginis canendo unum atque
> alterum psalmum Latinum, responsorium pro tempore et hymnum Magnificat. In reliquis autem
> templis Germanice canatur.

9. The day of Pentecost, together with the two joined to it. 10. The day of the Trinity. 11. The
   day of John the Baptist. 12. The day of the Visitation of Mary. 13. The day of Michael. On
   the vigil and preparation of these feasts, about the second hour, let vespers be held by the
   whole Latin school in the church of the Blessed Virgin, singing one or two Latin psalms, the
   respond for the season, and the hymn *Magnificat*. But in the rest of the churches let it be
   sung in German.

Nicolaus Hausmann's order for Anhalt is the only order in the corpus that would like to keep the
night vigil of Christmas and Easter. **Anhalt, Nicolaus Hausmann's order, 1532**
(Sehling 2, p. 542):

<!-- doc 1262 -->
> Vigilia paschce. natalis. Es wer auch nicht bose, das die christnacht und ostern mit der wache
> gehalden wurden, wie für alters.

The vigil of Easter; of the Nativity. It were also not evil that Christmas night and Easter were
kept with the watch, as of old.

**Note.** Hausmann goes on to name the abuses that have grown up around the night watch. He
proposes instead an early service at about three in the morning (p. 543).

---

### <a id="s12-5"></a>12.5 The Lutheran scale of feasts

#### <a id="s12-5-1"></a>12.5.1 The common pattern

Most orders rank the feast days in the same few steps, though the words vary.

| Rank | Names used in the orders | Usual days | How kept |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sunday | *der Sontag*, *des Herren Tag*, *dies dominica* | every Sunday | the whole day; the norm by which the feasts are measured |
| 1. The high feasts | *hohe Feste*, *Hauptfeste*, *heuptfest des herrn Christi*, *de dre groten feste Christi*, *summa festa*, *Vierzeiten*, *große Feste* | Christmas, Easter, Whitsunday, each with one or two following days; often Michaelmas as the fourth; sometimes Ascension | the whole day, usually on two or three days; two or three sermons; Latin chant, sequence and proper preface; figural music; communion; no weddings |
| 2. The other feasts of Christ and "Gospel" feasts | *die andern festa Christi*, *fürnembste Feste*, *andere herliche fest*, *gemeine fest*, *mittelmeßige festa* | Circumcision (New Year), Epiphany, Purification, Annunciation, Ascension, Trinity; John the Baptist, Visitation, Michaelmas; in some orders Maundy Thursday and Good Friday | usually the whole day, "as on Sundays", with the introit, sequence and preface *de tempore*; in some orders only the forenoon |
| 3. Apostles' days and other saints' days | *Aposteltage*, *kleine Feste*, *halbe Feiertage*, *festa apostolorum* | the apostles; the Conversion of Paul; often Mary Magdalene, the Beheading of John, All Saints | a sermon in the forenoon, work after it; or no holy day, with the Gospel preached on the next Sunday or at a weekday sermon |
| 4. Abolished feasts | *papistische feste*, *abgötterische feste* | Corpus Christi, Holy Cross, the Conception, Nativity and Assumption of Mary (in most orders), All Souls, local saints | not kept; sometimes proclaimed and explained so that people know why they are gone |

The orders differ in three ways:

- **How many ranks they draw.** Some have two, many three, and a few four.
- **Where the middle feasts stand.** John the Baptist, the Visitation, Michaelmas, and in some
  orders Purification and Annunciation, sit either with the feasts of Christ or with the
  apostles.
- **What a lower rank means.** It may mean a half holy day, a single sermon, a transfer to
  Sunday, or the loss of the holy day altogether.

The families below show the main lines.

#### <a id="s12-5-2"></a>12.5.2 The Saxon and Mecklenburg family: "over and above these chiefest feasts"

The line starts with the Saxon *Unterricht der Visitatoren* of 1528. It speaks of two ranks in
its own words.

**Saxony (Ernestine), *Unterricht der Visitatoren*, 1528** (Sehling 1, p. 164):

<!-- doc 9 -->
> Were auch gut, das sie eintrechtiglich feierten, die sontage, annunciationis, purificationis,
> visitationis der reinen jungfrauen Maria, S. Johannis des teufers, Michaelis, der aposteln,
> Magdalene, die selben feste weren denn bereit abgangen, und künten nicht bequemlich alle wider
> aufgericht werden. Und in sonderheit sol man halten den christag, beschneidung, epiphanie, die
> osterfeier, auffart, pfingsten, doch abgethan, was unchristlich legenden oder gesang darinnen
> gefunden werden.

It were good also that they should keep holy day with one accord on the Sundays, the
Annunciation, the Purification, the Visitation of the pure Virgin Mary, St John the Baptist,
Michaelmas, the apostles', Magdalene; unless those feasts be already fallen away and could not
conveniently all be set up again. And in especial one shall keep Christmas, the Circumcision,
the Epiphany, the Easter holy days, the Ascension, Whitsuntide; yet with all things done away
that are found therein of unchristian legends or chants.

In Albertine Saxony the feasts of Christ follow the preamble quoted in [§12.3.7](#s12-3-7). Sehling gives this
part of the order in his own summary but quotes the text. **Saxony (Albertine),
*Kirchenordnung*, 1539** (Sehling 1, p. 274):

<!-- doc 30 -->
> Der tag nativitatis oder der geburt Christi sampt den andern und auch dem dritten
> nechstfolgenden, so man daran communicanten hat. Der tag circumcisionis oder der beschneidung
> Christi. Der tag epiphanie, das ist der erscheinung oder offenbarung Christi, da die weisen
> aus morgenland durch erscheinung des sterns zu Christo kamen. Dieser tag wird auch gehalten
> von der taufe Christi. Der tag der offenbarung Christi in dem tempel, so man nennet
> purificationis Mariae. Der tag annuntiationis seu conceptionis Christi, da Christus in der
> jungfrauen leib empfangen ist. Der tag coenae domini, so man nennet den grünen donnerstag,
> daran von dem abendmal und hochwirdigen sakrament zu predigen ist. Der tag des leidens
> Christi, so der karfreitag genennet wird. Der ostertag von der auferstehung des herrn sampt
> dem nechstfolgenden und dritten, so man communicanten hat. Der tag der himelfart Christi. Der
> pfingstag von der sendung des heiligen geists. Der heiligen dreifaltigkeit fest gefellet auf
> den nehesten sontag nach pfingsten. Hierüber sollen auch diese fest gehalten werden. Der tag
> S. Johannis des teufers zu ehren dem heiligen predigampt des evangelii von Christo. Der tag
> visitationis, da Maria ire mume Elisabeth heimgesucht hat von wegen derselben historien des
> evangelii. Der tag Michaelis, daran von den heiligen engeln zu predigen. […] Man mag auch die
> tage der heiligen aposteln halten, das man vor mittag daran predige und, so es fürfelt, die
> communio halte. Nachmittage aber mag man wol der teglichen arbeit warten, oder, wo man wil,
> mag man die evangelia und gedechtnis von den heiligen aposteln auf die nehesten sontag, so
> darnach gefallen, zur mittags oder vesper predigt verlegen. Desgleichen mag es auch mit
> etlichen anderen festen der heiligen, welcher historien im evangelio beschrieben sind,
> gehalten werden, als da sind S. Paulus bekerung, Marie Magalena, S. Johannis enthauptung, S.
> Stephan etc.

The day of the Nativity or birth of Christ, with the second and also the third next following,
if there be communicants thereon. The day of the Circumcision of Christ. The day of the
Epiphany, that is, of the appearing or manifestation of Christ, when the wise men from the east
came to Christ by the appearing of the star; this day is also kept of the baptism of Christ. The
day of the manifestation of Christ in the temple, which is called the Purification of Mary. The
day of the Annunciation or Conception of Christ, when Christ was conceived in the Virgin's womb.
The day of the Lord's Supper, which is called Maundy Thursday, whereon one is to preach of the
Supper and the most worthy Sacrament. The day of the Passion of Christ, which is called Good
Friday. Easter day, of the resurrection of the Lord, with the next following and the third, if
there be communicants. The day of the Ascension of Christ. Whitsunday, of the sending of the
Holy Ghost. The feast of the holy Trinity falleth on the next Sunday after Pentecost. Over and
above these, these feasts also shall be kept: the day of St John the Baptist, to the honour of
the holy office of preaching the Gospel of Christ; the day of the Visitation, when Mary visited
her cousin Elisabeth, because of that history of the Gospel; the day of Michael, whereon one is
to preach of the holy angels. […] One may also keep the days of the holy apostles, so that one
preach thereon before noon and, if occasion serve, hold the communion. But in the afternoon one
may well attend to the daily work; or, if one will, one may put over the Gospels and remembrance
of the holy apostles to the next Sunday that followeth, to the midday or evening sermon.
Likewise it may be done also with certain other feasts of the saints whose histories are written
in the Gospel, as are St Paul's conversion, Mary Magdalene, St John's beheading, St Stephen,
etc.

The Merseburg synodal instruction sets the two ranks side by side, and its title for the lower
rank is a phrase worth noting: "doch ahne gebotene feir", without a commanded holy day.
**Merseburg, *Synodalunterricht*, 1544** (Sehling 2, p. 20):

<!-- doc 1211 -->
> Den ganzen tag zu feiren fur und nachmittage zu predigen: Alle sontage und volgende
> evangelische festa: nativitas Christi sampt dem andern auch dem dritten tage, so man daran
> communicanten hat […] Hiruber sollen dise feirtage gehalten werden: der tag S. Johannis des
> teufers zu ehren dem heiligen predigtampt des evangelii von Christo der tag visitationis, da
> die junkfrau Maria ihre muhme Elisabet heimgesucht hat von wegen der feinen historien des
> evangelii der tag Michaelis dar von den lieben engeln zu predigen. An volgenden tagen solle
> fur mittage predigt und communion, do es fur fiele, gehalten und die dem volk auf den sontag
> zuvor doch ahne gebotene feir vorkundiget werden. Als nemlich der tag cene domini, so man den
> grunen donnerstag nennet, daran von dem abentmahl und hochwirdigen sacrament zu predigen der
> tag des leidens Christi, so der karfreitag genennet wirt, dar man die ganz historia des
> leidens Christi dem volk furtragen solt der tag Petri und Pauli und aller apostel zu ehren des
> heiligen apostelampts

To keep holy day the whole day, and to preach before and after noon: all Sundays, and the
following evangelical feasts: the Nativity of Christ with the second and also the third day, if
there be communicants thereon […] Over and above these, these holy days shall be kept: the day
of St John the Baptist, to the honour of the holy office of preaching the Gospel of Christ; the
day of the Visitation, when the Virgin Mary visited her cousin Elisabeth, because of the fine
history of the Gospel; the day of Michael, whereon to preach of the dear angels. On the
following days preaching and communion, if it so fall out, shall be held before noon, and they
shall be declared to the people on the Sunday before, yet without a commanded holy day: namely
the day of the Lord's Supper, which is called Maundy Thursday, whereon to preach of the Supper
and the most worthy Sacrament; the day of the Passion of Christ, which is called Good Friday,
whereon the whole history of the Passion of Christ should be set forth to the people; the day of
Peter and Paul and of all apostles, to the honour of the holy apostolic office

**Note.** Maundy Thursday and Good Friday stand in the lower rank here, beside the apostles. The
feasts of Christ are placed by their standing as holy days, not by their theological weight.

The Mecklenburg order of 1552 is the fullest form of the Saxon scheme, and it is the one most
often copied. **Mecklenburg, *Kirchenordnung*, 1552** (Sehling 5, pp. 200–201):

<!-- doc 1922 -->
> Von den besondern festen oder feiertagen, so man im jar halten sol. Uber die gemeinen sontage
> sollen gehalten werden die hohen heubtfest des herrn Christi, als da sind. Der tag Nativitatis
> oder der geburt Christi, samt dem andern und dritten folgenden. Der tag Circumcisionis oder
> der beschneidung Christi. Der tag Epiphanie, das ist der erscheinung oder offenbarung Christi,
> den man nennet der heiligen drei könig tag. Der tag der opferung Christi im tempel, genant
> Purificationis Mariae. Der tag Annunciationis Mariae oder Conceptionis Christi, da Christus in
> der jungfrauen leib empfangen ist. Der tag Coenae domini, den man den grönen donnerstag
> nennet, daran von des herrn abendmal sol gepredigt werden. Der tag Passionis domini oder des
> leidens und sterbens Christi, welcher der karfreitag genennet wird. Der ostertag oder Pasca,
> der tag der ufferstehung Christi, samt dem folgenden montag und dienstag. Der tag Ascensionis
> oder himelfart Christi. Der pfingstag, samt dem folgenden montag und dienstag. Der tag
> Trinitatis gefelt uff den nehesten sontag nach pfingsten. Uff diese fest sol es mit ordnung
> der lection, gesange, predigten und communio gehalten werden, wie den gemeinen sontagen,
> allein, das die introitus, sequenz und prefationes de tempore gesungen werden. […] Uber diese
> furnemsten fest sollen auch die gehalten werden. Die tage der aposteln. Der tag S. Johannis
> des teufers. Der tag Visitationis, da Maria ire mume Elisabeth heimsucht. […] Der tag
> Michaelis, an welchem die lere von den heiligen engeln dem volk sol furgetragen werden. An
> diesen tagen sol man vor mittage predigen, und so communicanten da sind, die communion halten,
> wie an den sontagen. Nach mittage aber mag man wol der gewönlichen erbeit warten. Ausgenomen
> den tag Michaelis, an welchem vor und nach mittage sol gepredigt werden. Das fest aber
> Assumptionis, oder himelfart Marie, sol hinfurder ganz abgethan sein, und an des selben stat
> das fest S. Michaelis als ein viergezeiten fest gehalten werden.

Of the special feasts or holy days which shall be kept in the year. Over and above the common
Sundays shall be kept the high chief feasts of the Lord Christ, which are these: the day of the
Nativity or birth of Christ, with the second and third following; the day of the Circumcision of
Christ; the day of the Epiphany, that is, of the appearing or manifestation of Christ, which is
called the day of the Three Kings; the day of the offering of Christ in the temple, called the
Purification of Mary; the day of the Annunciation of Mary or Conception of Christ, when Christ
was conceived in the Virgin's womb; the day of the Lord's Supper, which is called Maundy
Thursday, whereon shall be preached of the Lord's Supper; the day of the Passion of the Lord, or
of the suffering and death of Christ, which is called Good Friday; Easter day, or Pascha, the
day of the resurrection of Christ, with the Monday and Tuesday following; the day of the
Ascension of Christ; Whitsunday, with the Monday and Tuesday following; the day of the Trinity
falleth on the next Sunday after Pentecost. On these feasts it shall be done, as touching the
order of lessons, chants, sermons and communion, as on the common Sundays; only that the
introits, sequences and prefaces *de tempore* be sung. […] Over and above these chiefest feasts
these also shall be kept: the days of the apostles; the day of St John the Baptist; the day of
the Visitation, when Mary visiteth her cousin Elisabeth; […] the day of Michael, whereon the
doctrine of the holy angels shall be set forth to the people. On these days one shall preach
before noon, and if there be communicants, hold the communion, as on Sundays; but in the
afternoon one may well attend to the wonted work. Except the day of Michael, whereon there shall
be preaching before and after noon. But the feast of the Assumption, or Ascension of Mary, shall
henceforth be wholly done away, and in the stead of the same the feast of St Michael be kept as
a feast of the four times.

**Note.** Michaelmas has a place of its own in this scheme:

- It is listed with the second rank, but it is preached "before and after noon" like a feast of
  Christ.
- It takes the Assumption's place as one of the four *Vierzeiten* ([§12.9](#s12-9)).

The Mecklenburg text, with small changes, stands in these orders:

| Order | Sehling | Changes of note |
|---|---|---|
| Pfalz-Zweibrücken, *Kirchenordnung*, 1557 | 18, pp. 205–206 | apostles' days not named one by one (listed in the *Feiertagsordnung* of 1561, [§12.6.2](#s12-6-2)) |
| Lüneburg, *Kirchenordnung*, 1564 | 6/1, pp. 550–551 | follows Mecklenburg closely, including the prefaces *de tempore* |
| Wolfenbüttel, *Kirchenordnung*, 1569 | 6/1, pp. 151–152 | "Aber an solchen apostelntagen nach der predigt mag ein jeder seiner arbeit woll warten"; Corpus Christi explicitly abolished |
| Oldenburg, *Kirchenordnung*, 1573 | 7/2.1, pp. 1096–1097 | Michaelmas "anstadt des fests assumtionis oder himelfart Mariae als ein viergezeitenfest"; Te Deum for the harvest |
| Lüneburg (city), *Kirchenordnung*, 1575 | 6/1, pp. 660–661 | as Lüneburg 1564 |
| Lippe, *Kirchenordnung*, 1571 | 21, pp. 391–392 | prefaces *de tempore* only "auff den Viergezeiten Festagen" ([§12.9](#s12-9)) |
| Verden, *Kirchenordnung*, 1606 | 7/1, p. 166 | Trinity "hochfeyerlich" |
| Waldeck, *Kirchenordnung*, 1556 | 9, pp. 272–273 | Michaelmas "fur das virte heuptfest"; Good Friday "halb feierlich biß auff den mittag" ([§12.6.1](#s12-6-1)) |
| Kronstadt (Transylvania), *Agende*, 1547 | 24, p. 255 | the list itself follows the Nürnberg model ([§12.5.7](#s12-5-7), [§12.8.3](#s12-8-3)); the closing admonition is taken from the Saxon order of 1539/40 |

#### <a id="s12-5-3"></a>12.5.3 The Württemberg family: holy days proclaimed by the magistrate

The Württemberg orders make the magistrate's proclamation the mark of a holy day ([§12.3.5](#s12-3-5)). At
first they drew only one clear line: the high feasts of Christ kept the whole day, and the rest
kept only in the forenoon.

**Württemberg, *Kirchenordnung*, 1536** (Sehling 16, pp. 105–106):

<!-- doc 651 -->
> Es sollen aber in unserm Fürstenthumb nachvolgende fest- und feyrtag gehalten werden: Erstlich
> alle Sontag, Item, alle hohe fest Christi als namlich Weyhennächt, Beschneidung, Ostertag,
> Auffarttag, Pfingstag. Und sollen dise tag doch auch ungefar gehalten und niemand sein
> gewissen damit beschwert werden […] Weiter aber sollen all pfarrer auff nachverzeichnet tag
> morgens predigen und als dann dem volck anzeigen, das sich nachmittag meniglich an sein arbeit
> verfügen möge unnd hierinn niemandt verstrickt sein sol. Namlich auff der heiligen drey künig
> oder den zwölfften tag, da soll man predigen aus dem Mattheo das ander Capitel, den grünen
> donnerstag, den karfreitag, so man den passion prediget, unser frawen verkündung tag
> Annuntiationis, unnser frawen Reynigung Purificationis, aller apostel tag, Sant Johannis des
> täuffers tag.

But in our principality the feasts and holy days following shall be kept: first all Sundays;
item, all the high feasts of Christ, namely Christmas, the Circumcision, Easter day, Ascension
day, Whitsunday. And these days also shall be kept without constraint, and no man's conscience
burdened therewith […] But further, all parsons shall preach in the morning on the days
hereafter noted, and then shew the people that every man may betake himself to his work in the
afternoon, and that herein no man shall be bound: namely on the day of the Three Kings or
Twelfth Day, whereon shall be preached out of Matthew the second chapter; Maundy Thursday; Good
Friday, when the Passion is preached; our Lady's Annunciation day; our Lady's Purification; all
apostles' days; St John the Baptist's day.

The Württemberg list follows the preamble of [§12.3.5](#s12-3-5). **Württemberg, *Kirchenordnung*, 1553**
(Sehling 16, p. 266):

<!-- doc 671 -->
> Alle Sontag Der Christag Der nächst tag darnach Der Jars tag Der öberst, Epiphania genannt Der
> Ostertag sampt dem nächsten darnach Die himelfart Christi Der Pfingstag sampt volgendem Montag
> Die Liechtmeß Purificationis Mariae Verkündigung Mariae, genannt Annunciationis Aller Aposteln
> tag Joannis Baptisten

All Sundays. Christmas day. The next day after. New Year's day. Twelfth Day, called the
Epiphany. Easter day with the next after. The Ascension of Christ. Whitsunday with the Monday
following. Candlemas, the Purification of Mary. The Annunciation of Mary. All apostles' days.
John the Baptist's.

**Note.** In 1553 every day on the list is a holy day, with no half days. The distinction came
back in later orders of the family:

- **Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1561** added half days ([§12.6.2](#s12-6-2)).
- **Pfalz-Veldenz 1574** added half days as well ([§12.6.2](#s12-6-2)).
- **Baden 1603** has the same list but allows field-work after the morning service:

**Baden, *Kirchenordnungsmandat*, 1603** (Sehling 16, p. 559):

<!-- doc 715 -->
> Die Sontag seyndt aller dings stricte zufeyren undt alle Feldt- und andere arbeit
> einzustellen, zugleich auch die ordentliche Fest- und Aposteltag vormittag simpliciter
> gefeyret, nachmittag allein mit der discretion zur Feldtarbeit zugelaßen werden soll

The Sundays are to be kept holy altogether strictly, and all field-work and other labour to
cease; likewise the ordinary feast days and apostles' days shall be kept holy in the forenoon
without condition, and in the afternoon field-work shall be allowed only with discretion

#### <a id="s12-5-4"></a>12.5.4 The Bugenhagen family: "the three great feasts of Christ"

Bugenhagen's orders count feasts from the three great feasts of Christ. Each is kept three full
days. The rest are "full" holy days for their Gospel histories. The apostles are commemorated on
the next Sunday.

**Braunschweig, *Kirchenordnung*, 1528** (Sehling 6/1, p. 397):

<!-- doc 1983 -->
> De dre groten feste Christi, de de Christene stedes hebben geholden, alse Winachten, Paschen
> unde Pynxten, eyn jewelick fest dre dage vullen to vyren, darinne geprediget schal werden up
> den morgen, vor middage, na middage unde up den avent, darto gesungen, alse na gesecht schal
> werden. Darto nyejarsdach, Epiphanie, dat is der apenbaringe edder koningedach,
> purificationis, dat is Marien kerckgank, Marien vorkundinge, des Heren hemmelvart, Joannis
> Baptiste, Marien berchgank vullen to vyren, nicht umme der dage willen, sonder umme des
> predigens willen, dewile de historien in den evangelien begrepen synt unde bedrapen unsen
> Heren Christum etc. Item Michaelis vor eyn vehrtidenvest, to offeren dat vehrtidenoffer in de
> gemeyne schatkaste, ock vullen to vyren. […] Der hilgen apostelen unde Magdalene unde
> Laurentii, des hilgen kastenheren edder diakens, gedechtnissen scholen gelecht werden up den
> negesten Sundach na öreme kalenderdage, also dat me vlitich predigen schal dat evangelium
> vamme Sundage alse up eynen anderen Sundach unde deme jo nichts affbreken; alle sank unde
> misse schal ock syn vamme Sundage, alleyne amme ende des sermons schal de predicante seggen:
> Myne frunde in Christo, in disser weke plecht me gedenken des hilgen apostels N., van deme
> lest me so in evangelio, in Actis apo. etc.

The three great feasts of Christ which the Christians have always kept, as Christmas, Easter and
Whitsuntide, every feast to be fully kept holy three days, wherein there shall be preaching in
the morning, before noon, after noon and at evening, and singing thereto, as shall be said
hereafter. Thereto New Year's day, the Epiphany, that is the day of the manifestation or the
Kings' day, the Purification, that is Mary's church-going, Mary's Annunciation, the Lord's
Ascension, John the Baptist, Mary's going over the hills, to be fully kept holy; not for the
days' sake, but for the preaching's sake, forasmuch as the histories are contained in the
Gospels and concern our Lord Christ, etc. Item, Michaelmas for a feast of the four times, to
offer the four-times offering into the common treasure-chest, also to be fully kept holy. […]
The memorials of the holy apostles, and of Magdalene, and of Laurence the holy chest-master or
deacon, shall be laid upon the next Sunday after their calendar day; so that one shall
diligently preach the Gospel of the Sunday as upon another Sunday, and take nothing at all from
it; all chant and mass also shall be of the Sunday; only at the end of the sermon the preacher
shall say: My friends in Christ, in this week it is wont to be remembered of the holy apostle
N., of whom one readeth thus in the Gospel, in the Acts of the apostles, etc.

**Note.**

- **Why the apostles lost their holy day.** The editor records that Bugenhagen first meant to
  keep the apostles' days as feasts. He gave up the plan when it was objected that a town of
  craftsmen would then have too many holy days.
- **Hamburg 1529.** Hamburg has the same text (Sehling 5, p. 514).
- **Lübeck 1531.** Lübeck adds the list of the four times ([§12.9](#s12-9)).

**Pomerania, *Kirchenordnung*, 1535** (Sehling 4, p. 343):

<!-- doc 1856 -->
> Unde de historien van unserm leven heren Jesu Christo nicht vorgeten werden, wille wi de festa
> Christi alle beholden, als winachten dree dage, osteren dree dage, pinxsten dree dage, dar
> negest Circuncisionis, Epiphanie, Purificationis, Annunciationis, Ascensionis, Trinitatis,
> Johannis Baptiste to predekende, van siner entfanginge, van siner gebort, van sinem predekende
> unde amt, unde van siner enthovedinge, dat fest hört ock up Christum, unde de historie is ock
> in den evangelien geschreven. Visitationis des geliken. Item wi willen ock beholden dat fest
> Michaelis to predikende van den engeln ut der hiligen schrift.

And that the histories of our dear Lord Jesus Christ be not forgotten, we will keep all the
feasts of Christ: as Christmas three days, Easter three days, Whitsuntide three days; next
thereafter the Circumcision, the Epiphany, the Purification, the Annunciation, the Ascension,
the Trinity; John the Baptist, to preach of his conception, of his birth, of his preaching and
office, and of his beheading, for that feast also pertaineth to Christ, and the history is also
written in the Gospels. The Visitation likewise. Item, we will also keep the feast of Michael,
to preach of the angels out of holy Scripture.

The Schleswig-Holstein list follows the principle quoted in [§12.3.3](#s12-3-3). **Schleswig-Holstein,
*Kirchenordnung*, 1542** (Sehling 23, p. 95):

<!-- doc 1576 -->
> De dre groten Feste Christi vyren wy ein ytlick dre dage lanck umme der Historien Christi
> willen. Darbeneven vyren wy ock dat Fest Circumcisionis, Epiphaniae, Purificationis unde
> Annunctiationis Marie. […] Ock vyre wy de Festa Ascensionis und Visitationis […] Thom lesten
> dat fest Johannis Baptiste, Dat fest Michaelis thor dancksegginge Unde dat fest Omnium
> Sanctorum. Der Apostel Feste schal men apentlick affkündigen und thogelick dem feste Magdalene
> unde Laurentii am negst volgenden Sondage darna Predigen.

The three great feasts of Christ we keep holy each three days long, for the histories of Christ.
Beside these we keep holy also the feast of the Circumcision, of the Epiphany, of the
Purification and of the Annunciation of Mary. […] We keep holy also the feasts of the Ascension
and of the Visitation […] Last of all the feast of John the Baptist, the feast of Michael for
thanksgiving, and the feast of All Saints. The apostles' feasts one shall openly proclaim, and
preach them, together with the feast of Magdalene and of Laurence, on the next following Sunday
thereafter.

**Note.** The editor explains the "Festa Ascensionis" as the Assumption of Mary, on 15 August.
The Danish-Holstein order of 1542 is thus one of the few Lutheran orders that keeps the
Assumption as a holy day ([§12.8.3](#s12-8-3)). The Kiel draft behind it follows the Danish *Ordinatio
ecclesiastica* of 1537.

#### <a id="s12-5-5"></a>12.5.5 Numbered classes

Some orders number their ranks outright.

Grubenhagen names three classes, and gives each its reason. **Grubenhagen, *Kirchenordnung*,
1544** (Sehling 6/2, pp. 1032–1033):

<!-- doc 2056 -->
> VI. Von den feyertagen, welche man feyeren soll. Festum nativitatis Christi, S. Stephanstagk,
> des ersten merterers, S. Johannistagk, des evangelisten, der unschuldigen kinderlein tagk,
> weil die predigt wart, festum resurrectionis Christi, den Mondagk und auch den Dinstagk,
> festum Pentecostae, Pfingsten, den Mondagk und auch den Dinstagk zu feyeren, festum Michaelis
> archangeli. Das sind also die vier hauptfest, an welchen man den vierzeitpenning sammelt. Nun
> folgen andere herliche fest, die man auch feyren soll: Festum circumcisionis Domini, f.
> epiphaniae vel trium regum, f. purificationis Mariae, f. anuntiacionis Mariae, f. visitationis
> Mariae, f. ascensionis Jesu Christi, f. S. Johannis Baptistae. Das sind also andere sieben
> festage, die auch zum hochsten von wegen der historien zu feyren nottig. 1. S. Andres tagk, 2.
> S. Thomas tagk, 3. S. Matthias tagk, 4. den grünen Donnerstagk, 5. den stillen Freytagk, 6. S.
> Philippi et Jacobi tagk, 7. S. Petri et Pauli tagk, 8. S. […] Jacobs tagk, 9. S. Bartholomei
> tagk, 10. S. Matthäi apostoli tagk, 11. S. Simonis et Judä tagk. Diese tage der lieben
> heiligen und jünger unsers Hern Jesu Christi soll man vormittage alleine, weil das ampt wart,
> schuldig sein zu feyren.

VI. Of the holy days which shall be kept. The feast of the Nativity of Christ; St Stephen's day,
of the first martyr; St John's day, of the evangelist; the day of the innocent children, while
the sermon lasteth; the feast of the resurrection of Christ, the Monday and also the Tuesday;
the feast of Pentecost, Whitsuntide, the Monday and also the Tuesday to be kept holy; the feast
of Michael the archangel. These are therefore the four chief feasts, whereon the four-times
penny is gathered. Now follow other glorious feasts, which shall also be kept holy: the feast of
the Circumcision of the Lord; the feast of the Epiphany or of the Three Kings; the feast of the
Purification of Mary; the feast of the Annunciation of Mary; the feast of the Visitation of
Mary; the feast of the Ascension of Jesus Christ; the feast of St John the Baptist. These are
therefore seven other feast days, which also are in the highest degree needful to be kept holy
because of the histories. 1. St Andrew's day, 2. St Thomas's day, 3. St Matthias's day, 4.
Maundy Thursday, 5. Good Friday, 6. St Philip and James's day, 7. St Peter and Paul's day, 8. St
[…] James's day, 9. St Bartholomew's day, 10. St Matthew the apostle's day, 11. St Simon and
Jude's day. These days of the dear saints and disciples of our Lord Jesus Christ one shall be
bound to keep holy in the forenoon only, while the office lasteth.

**Note.** The first class is defined partly by a church payment. The four chief feasts are the
days on which the four-times penny is collected ([§12.9](#s12-9)). The Ascension stands in the second class,
and Maundy Thursday and Good Friday in the third. The editor notes that this departs from the
Wolfenbüttel order of 1543, which moved the apostles' days to the next Sunday.

**Regensburg, *Kirchenordnung*, 1567** (Sehling 13, p. 474):

<!-- doc 450 -->
> [5.] Welche fest in unserer kirchen gefeiert werden. Uber die gemeinen sontäge werden mit
> verstand christlicher freiheit gehalten: Erstlich alle festa Christi: Nativitatis mit den
> volgenden zweien tagen, Circumcisionis, Epiphaniae, Purificationis, Annunciationis, Ostertag
> samt den zweien nachvolgenden tagen, Ascensionis, Pfingstag sampt den volgenden zweien tagen.
> Zum andern werden gehalten alle aposteltage. Zum dritten: Johannis baptistae, Michaelis
> archangeli.

[5.] Which feasts are kept holy in our church. Over and above the common Sundays are kept, with
understanding of Christian liberty: first, all the feasts of Christ: the Nativity with the two
days following, the Circumcision, the Epiphany, the Purification, the Annunciation, Easter day
with the two days next following, the Ascension, Whitsunday with the two days following.
Secondly are kept all the apostles' days. Thirdly: John the Baptist, Michael the archangel.

**Note.** Regensburg's numbering is an order of listing, not of dignity. Communion and first
vespers, which mark the rank in this order, are given only "an festen Christi, allen und jeden",
on each and every feast of Christ (p. 475; see [§12.10.9](#s12-10-9)).

Hoya has four ranks, the fourth being the abolished Assumption. **Hoya, *Kirchenordnung*, 1571**
(Sehling 6/2, p. 1186):

<!-- doc 2065 -->
> Die vier hohen fest belangende, ordnen wir, das Weynachten, Ostern, Pfingsten mit den zweyen
> folgenden tagen sollen geruhet, gefeyert und mit übung göttliches worts zugebracht werden.
> Dieweil aber das fest der himelfart Mariae ohne grund und gezeugnis der schrift durch den
> antichrist eingefüret ist, sol es in unser graffschaft hiemit ganz abgethan sein und seiner
> hinfüro nicht gedacht werden. Wir ordnen aber anstadt desselben das fest S. Michaelis und
> wollen, das die pfarrkinder den tag feyerlich halten, auch ihrem pastorn an demselben tage ihr
> opfer und gebürliche pflicht gütlich entrichten und ohne hindernis dargeben sollen. Zum andern
> ordnen wir, das nachgeschriebene und verzeichnete fest und tage in unser herrschaft genzlich
> geruhet, gefeyret und geheiliget werden sollen, als des neuen jhars tag, der heiligen drey
> könig tag, das festum purificationis Mariae, verkündigung Mariae, der himelfart Christi,
> Johannis des teufers tag, visitationis Mariae, der tag coenae Domini, an welchem man vom h.
> nachtmal predigen sol, den Kahrfreytag […] Zum dritten ordnen wir, das man nachgesetzte
> apostel- und heiligentage, biß die serrnon geendet, feyren sol: als Andreae Thomae bekerung
> Pauli Matthiae Petri et Pauli Philippi et Jacobi Magdalenen Jacobi Bartholomaei decollationis
> Johannis Matthaei Simonis et Judae aller heiligen tag.

As touching the four high feasts, we ordain that Christmas, Easter and Whitsuntide, with the two
days following, shall be rested, kept holy, and spent in the exercise of God's Word. But
forasmuch as the feast of the Ascension of Mary was brought in by the Antichrist without ground
and witness of Scripture, it shall hereby be wholly done away in our county, and no more be
mentioned henceforth. But in the stead thereof we ordain the feast of St Michael, and will that
the parishioners keep the day solemnly, and also render to their pastor on the same day their
offering and due duty kindly and without hindrance. Secondly we ordain that the feasts and days
hereafter written and set down shall in our lordship be wholly rested, kept holy and hallowed:
as New Year's day, the day of the Three Kings, the feast of the Purification of Mary, the
Annunciation of Mary, the Ascension of Christ, John the Baptist's day, the Visitation of Mary,
the day of the Lord's Supper, whereon one shall preach of the holy Supper, Good Friday […]
Thirdly we ordain that the apostles' and saints' days hereafter set shall be kept holy until the
sermon be ended: as Andrew, Thomas, the Conversion of Paul, Matthias, Peter and Paul, Philip and
James, Magdalene, James, Bartholomew, the Beheading of John, Matthew, Simon and Jude, All
Saints' day.

The Harlingerland order repeats Hoya's text, divided into titled *Sectiones*. **Harlingerland
(East Frisia), *Kirchenordnung*, 1573/74** (Sehling 7/1, pp. 735–736):

<!-- doc 2122 -->
> Der eilfte articull. Von den festen. Sectio prima. Von den vier zeiten. Die vier hohen
> festtage belangende, ordnen wir auch, daß Wihnachten, Paschen, Pfingsten mit den zween
> folgenden tagen sollen gerouwet, gefyret und mit öving deß gottlichen wordeß geheiliget
> werden. Von der himmelfahrt Mariae. Dieweile daß fest ohne grund und gezeugniß der schrift
> durch dem antechrist ist angerichtet, soll idt ganz abgetaen sein und seiner nit gedacht
> werden. Ordnen derohalben, daß der [!] letzste und vierte hochfesttagzeit solle S. Michaelis
> tag sein. […] Sectio secunda. Von den fürnembsten festtagen. […] Sectio tertia. Von den
> aposteltagen. Ordnen wir, daß man undergeschrieben aposteltage, beht der sermön geendiget,
> fihren solle

The eleventh article. Of the feasts. Section the first. Of the four times. As touching the four
high feast days, we ordain also that Christmas, Easter and Whitsuntide, with the two days
following, shall be rested, kept holy and hallowed with the exercise of the divine Word. Of the
Ascension of Mary. Forasmuch as that feast was set up by the Antichrist without ground and
witness of the Scripture, it shall be wholly done away and not be mentioned. We ordain therefore
that the last and fourth high feast-tide shall be St Michael's day. […] Section the second. Of
the chiefest feast days. […] Section the third. Of the apostles' days. We ordain that the
apostles' days underwritten shall be kept holy until the sermon be ended

Sayn has four classes, set out as a principle before the list. The margin heads the paragraph
*Festa quadrupli*. **Sayn, *Kirchenzuchtordnung*, 1582** (Sehling 19/1, p. 368):

<!-- doc 1090 -->
> Unndt konden die festen durch gantze jahr in viererley artt oder underschiedliche hauffe
> getheilt werden: 1. Etzliche festa, das seind haubtfesta also zu nennen, die man solenniter
> den gantzen tag feieren unndt darauff die gemeine wochentliche arbeit soll underlaßen werden.
> 2. Die ander seind nur mittelmeßige festa, die da halb gefeiret werden also unndt der gestalt,
> das man vormittag zur kirchen komme, predigt haltte unnd hör, nach mittag aber in
> wochentlicher abeit vortfahre. 3. Die dritte festag könnenn ohn nachteil unndt ergernus
> verlegt unndt auffgehoben werden auf den gemeinen bettag, so sonst in der wochen zur predigt
> deputirt unndt geordenet ist. 4. Die viertten festtage, so zu bestettigung offentlicher
> abgotterei im bapstumb eingefuhrt unndt gehalten worden, sollen in unserm evangelischen
> kirchen gar abgeschafft unndt underlaßen werden.

And the feasts through the whole year might be divided into four kinds or several companies:
1. Some feasts are to be called chief feasts, which men shall keep holy solemnly the whole day,
   and whereon the common weekly work shall be left off. 2. The others are but middling feasts,
   which are kept half holy, in this wise and manner, that men come to church in the forenoon,
   hold and hear a sermon, but in the afternoon go on in the weekly work. 3. The third feast
   days may without hurt and offence be removed and taken up upon the common day of prayer,
   which otherwise is deputed and ordained in the week for preaching. 4. The fourth feast days,
   which were brought in and kept in the papacy for the confirming of open idolatry, shall in
   our evangelical churches be wholly done away and left off.

The list attached to it. **Sayn, *Kirchenzuchtordnung*, 1582** (Sehling 19/1, pp. 372–373):

<!-- doc 1090 -->
> Hauptvesta, so den gantzen tagh feierlich gehalten undt daruff die gemeine wochentliche arbeit
> soll underlassen werdenn. Der heilige christagh. S. Stephani tagh. S. Joannis tag vormittagh.
> Der neue jars tag vor- und nachmittagh. Epiphania Domini oder der heiligen drey konig tag.
> Purificationis Mariae oder liechtmeß. Annunciationis Mariae oder conceptionis christi, welches
> fest, so es in der marterwoch oder nach ostern gefelt, sol es auf den sonabend palmarum stets
> gelegt werden. Der ostertag sampt den zweien nachvolgenden, montag und dienstagh. Der
> himelfartstag Christi durch auß. Der pfingstag und beide volgende, montag und dinstag in
> pfingsten. Das fest der heiligen dreyfaltigkeit, so allwege acht tage nach pfingsten volget.
> […] Der tag Johannis des täuffers. S. Michaels tag, dar man pfleget von den h. engeln zu
> predigen und gott fur den guten schutz der guten geister zu dancken. Nachvolgende tage werden
> nur halb gefeiret also und der gestalt, das man vor mittage zur kirchen komme, predigt halte
> und hore, nach mittag aber in wochentlicher arbeit fortfahre. Alle apostel tage sollen
> gehalten werden, wen undt wie sie des jars fallen, doch allein mit einer predigt vormittag
> halb feierlich. Der aposteln tage sollen gleich geachtet und fur halbe feiertag gerechnet
> werden: Der grüne donnerstag […] Der charfreitag […] Pauli bekehrungstag umb der furtreflichen
> historien willen. Mariae visitationis oder heimsuchungfest. Diese volgende und dergleichen
> tage mogen auf denn verordenten bettagen in der wochen geleget werden, als: S. Laurentii tagh.
> S. Marci, des evangelisten. S. Lucas, des evangelisten. […] Vincula Petri. Decollationis
> Joannis Baptistae. […] Aller heyligen, omnium sanctorum. Mariae Magdalenen fest umb der
> schonen text und historien willen, so daruf zue handlen verordnet, damit [sie] in gedechtnus
> bleiben. Unten verzeichnete tag sollen gar abgeschaft und underlaßen werden, als die da zur
> abgotterey und aberglauben anleitung und vorschub geben. Alle Marienfest, sie haben nahmen wie
> sie wollen, welche hiebevor nicht benennet worden. Sonderlich aber festum conceptionis,
> nativitatis, praesentationis, assumptionis Mariae sollen in unsern evangelischen kürchen gar
> auffgehoben und abe sein

Chief feasts, which shall be kept solemnly the whole day, and whereon the common weekly work
shall be left off. The holy Christmas day. St Stephen's day. St John's day in the forenoon. New
Year's day, before and after noon. The Epiphany of the Lord, or the day of the Three Kings. The
Purification of Mary, or Candlemas. The Annunciation of Mary, or Conception of Christ; which
feast, if it fall in the week of the Passion or after Easter, shall always be laid on the
Saturday before Palm Sunday. Easter day with the two following, Monday and Tuesday. The day of
the Ascension of Christ, throughout. Whitsunday and both the following, Monday and Tuesday in
Whitsuntide. The feast of the holy Trinity, which followeth always eight days after Pentecost.
[…] The day of John the Baptist. St Michael's day, whereon men are wont to preach of the holy
angels and to thank God for the good protection of the good spirits. The days following are kept
but half holy, in this wise and manner, that men come to church before noon, hold and hear a
sermon, but in the afternoon go on in the weekly work. All apostles' days shall be kept, when
and as they fall in the year, yet only with one sermon in the forenoon, half holy. With the
apostles' days shall be counted alike, and reckoned for half holy days: Maundy Thursday […] Good
Friday […] St Paul's conversion day, for the excellent history's sake. The feast of Mary's
Visitation. These days following, and the like, may be laid on the appointed days of prayer in
the week: as St Laurence's day; St Mark the evangelist's; St Luke the evangelist's; […] Peter's
Chains; the Beheading of John the Baptist; […] All Saints; Mary Magdalene's feast, for the sake
of the fair text and history appointed to be handled thereon, that [they] may remain in
remembrance. The days noted beneath shall be wholly done away and left off, as those that give
occasion and furtherance to idolatry and superstition: all feasts of Mary, be their names what
they will, which have not been named heretofore; but in especial the feasts of the Conception,
Nativity, Presentation and Assumption of Mary shall in our evangelical churches be wholly taken
up and be gone

**Note.** This is the fullest four-rank system in the corpus. The Sayn *Kirchenordnung* of 1590
(Sehling 19/1, p. 389) later reduced it to a single list of holy days, with the harvest apostles
kept in the forenoon only ([§12.6.4](#s12-6-4)).

The Aschersleben town agenda has a middle rank of eight feasts over and above the three chief
feasts. **Aschersleben, *Kirchen-Agenda*, 1575** (Sehling 2, p. 479):

<!-- doc 1260 -->
> Uber die drei heubtfeste, sollen auch in dieser christlichen gemeinde diese nachfolgende
> gehalten werden. 1. Circumcisionis domini. 2. Epiphanias domini. 3. Purificationis Mariae. 4.
> Annunciationis Mariae. 5. Ascensionis domini. 6. Johannis baptistae. 7. Visitationis Mariae,
> 8. Michaelis. In diesen festen soll es durchaus, wie an sontagen gehalten werden, allein das
> mit singen und predigen auf die fest gesehen und figurirt werde. […] Von den festis
> apostolorum. Andreae, Thomae, Matthiae, Philippi Jacobi, Petri et Pauli, Jacobi, Bartholomaei,
> Matthaei, Simonis et Judae: Sollen in unser gemeine fruehe eine predigt und das officium
> gehalten werden vormittage alleine. Die arbeitsleute aber mögen ein jeder seiner hantierung
> warten

Over and above the three chief feasts, these following shall also be kept in this Christian
congregation: 1. The Circumcision of the Lord. 2. The Epiphany of the Lord. 3. The Purification
of Mary. 4. The Annunciation of Mary. 5. The Ascension of the Lord. 6. John the Baptist. 7. The
Visitation of Mary. 8. Michael. On these feasts it shall be done throughout as on Sundays; only
that in singing and preaching regard be had to the feast, and that figural music be used. […] Of
the feasts of the apostles. Andrew, Thomas, Matthias, Philip and James, Peter and Paul, James,
Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon and Jude: in our congregation there shall be held early a sermon and
the office, before noon only. But the working people may each attend to his handiwork

#### <a id="s12-5-6"></a>12.5.6 Great feasts and small feasts: Danzig and Thorn

In Danzig the rank of a feast was marked above all by the bells ([§12.10.7](#s12-10-7)). The church fathers of
St Mary's set down the custom in 1612. Article 16 lists every feast of the year as *ein gross
fest* or *ein klein fest*.

**Danzig, St Mary's, *Kirchenordnung*, 1612** (Sehling 4, pp. 203–204):

<!-- doc 1844 -->
> Art. 14. Vom beigern auf die grossen feste. Wan ein gross fest einfellet, welches allezeit mit
> drei predigten gehalten wird, alsdan wird des tages zuvor vormittage geleutet, wie sonst auf
> den tag in der woche gebreuchlich. […] Art. 15. Wie man auf die kleinen feste beigert. Auf die
> kleinen feste, welche allzeit nur mit einer predigt gehalten werden, es sei dan, das etwa
> eines auf einen sontag einfeilet, oder vom sontage dahin verlegt wird, alsdann wird des tages
> zuvor nach mittage, wen es eins geschlagen hat, mit der Dominical und Apostolica gebeigert und
> mit der Osanna darein geleutet und dis heisset man mit der Osanna beiern […] Art. 16. Namen
